knowledge_point.title: Calculating a Matrix Product Using the Distributive Law

question.:question/worked-solution:
We apply the distributive law

$$
AB+CB=(A+C)B.
$$

So, we calculate $A+C$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}A+C & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -5 & -1 \\ -9 & 10 & 11\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-5 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 \\ 9 & -10 & -13\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{bmatrix} \\  & =-2{I}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AB+CB & =(A+C)B \\  & =-2{I}_{3}B \\  & =-2B \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}- 2 \sqrt{2} & -2 & - 2 \sqrt{3} \\ -2 & - 2 \sqrt{5} & -2 \\ - 2 \sqrt{7} & -2 & - 2 \sqrt{2}\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$
